intro: Outlook for mortgage loan officers on Mac comes down to three things: the right version, a few templates for the emails you repeat, and rules that keep title and borrower threads sorted. This page covers each one with menu paths and shortcuts you can use today. Lazur can also talk you through the steps while you work, one click at a time.
tldr: Check your version first. New Outlook for Mac is the default, and Microsoft says legacy support ends in October 2026.
Build templates for status requests, document follow-ups, and realtor check-ins. Built-in templates need Outlook for Mac 15.35 or later.
Use Shift+⌘F for search and Snooze for underwriting conditions that wait on other people.
Test every rule on a few old messages before you trust it. A June 2026 Microsoft Q&A thread reports rules that stopped working.
Lazur can talk you through these steps out loud while Outlook stays in front of you.

blocks.text: Most of a mortgage loan officer's day runs through the inbox. Borrower questions, document requests, realtor notes, title company replies, and closing details all land in the same place. This guide stays with Outlook for Mac, since that is the app this page covers. The tips assume a Mac and a Microsoft 365 account. If your company runs a different mail system, check with your IT team before you change settings.
Check which Outlook for Mac you are running

Start with the version. Microsoft makes new Outlook for Mac the default. A Legacy Outlook switch controls which experience you use. Turn the switch off to use the new experience. You can go back with Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook.

rows: Microsoft's latest listed feature release is 16.114, from Oct 14, 2026.
New Outlook is the default. Microsoft says legacy support ends in October 2026.
macOS 14 is the minimum for receiving Microsoft 365 and Office updates.
blocks.caption: Three checks before you change any settings.

blocks.title: Legacy has an end date
blocks.text: Microsoft says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026, and continued support depends on your license. The sources disagree on the exact date your mailbox stops connecting. Ask your IT team which date applies to your account.

Accounts do not move between versions on their own. An account added in one version is not automatically added to the other. If you switch, check your mail, calendar, and contacts before you rely on the new setup during a closing week.
Where loan officer email actually comes from
A mortgage broker blog lists the main sources of email load. Knowing the pattern helps you decide what to template, what to sort with rules, and what to snooze.

items: Borrower status requests: the same question about the same file, asked again and again.
Document collection: missing or incorrect documents, followed up until they arrive.
Realtor check-ins: short messages that still affect the deal and the timeline.
Title company threads: long chains with many recipients and attachments.
Underwriting conditions: letters with deadlines you must track and answer.
Closing instructions: final details that can stall a funding date if they slip.

blocks.text: The same blog uses a simple example. Writing a status request takes seconds, but you send the same one many times a week. The point holds. The blog does not measure how much time this work takes, and I did not find a study that does. Track your own week for a few days instead.
Save your repeat emails as templates in Outlook for Mac

Built-in templates are the cleanest option for repeat emails. They need a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac 15.35 or later. Microsoft lists them for Outlook for Microsoft 365, Outlook 2024, and Outlook 2021 for Mac.

items: Write the email once. Put placeholders in square brackets, such as [Borrower name] and [Property address].
Choose File > Save As Template.
Give the file a clear name, such as Status request, and save it.
To use it later, choose File > New > Mail From Template and pick the file. Templates save as .emltpl files.

blocks.text: Start with the status request, the missing document follow-up, the realtor check-in, and the closing reminder. Keep each one short. A template that needs a long rewrite saves no time. Here is a status request you can adapt:
Hi [Borrower name], I am checking on your file for [Property address]. Could you send your most recent bank statements by [Date]? Thank you, [Your name].
Remove real borrower details before you save a template. A template that still holds an old borrower's name is a privacy mistake waiting to happen.
Use the My Templates add-in when your company runs Exchange

The My Templates add-in is a separate option. It works only with Microsoft Exchange accounts. It is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. To make one, choose New Mail > My Templates > +Template in the task pane. If the add-in is missing, an organization admin may have turned add-ins off.

blocks.text: If you can use both, pick the built-in option first. Use the add-in only when your Exchange setup and admin policy allow it. Either way, test the template by sending it to yourself before a real borrower gets it.
Find borrower threads with search and filters
Search is the tool you will use most. Press Shift+⌘F to jump to search in new Outlook for Mac. Type a borrower's last name, a loan number, or a property address. Then narrow the results with filters.

Search by loan number first when you can. A loan number is more exact than a name, and a common name can appear in several files. Save the search habit for the busy weeks, when you need the old thread fast.
Some users report that search stopped working after the move to new Outlook. Test it on a thread you know before a busy week, so you find the problem early.
Build rules that sort title and realtor mail

Rules sort mail before you see it. A common setup moves title company emails into one folder and realtor emails into another. For the steps, read the [rules guide](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook). Then test the rule on a few old messages.

blocks.title: Test rules before a closing
blocks.text: A Microsoft Q&A thread from June 2026 reports that rules and junk-mail reporting stopped working for some users. Check that a rule still moves mail before you rely on it for a closing.
Keep rules simple. Match one sender or one phrase per rule. A complex rule is hard to debug when a file is already late.
Snooze underwriting conditions and follow-ups
Some mail waits on other people. An underwriting condition waits on a borrower. A payoff question waits on a title officer. Snooze hides a message until the time you choose, then it comes back.

Snooze is for mail you cannot act on yet. For a hard deadline, add a calendar event or an Apple Reminder too. Lazur can add the reminder by voice, and you can link the reminder back to the email. The [reminder guide](/how-to/set-a-reminder-for-an-email-in-outlook) shows the Outlook side.
The common mistake is snoozing everything. The snoozed pile then hides the mail that matters most. Snooze only what waits on someone else.
Calendar, My Day, and closing dates

Closing dates belong on your calendar. Press Shift+⌘] to open My Day, a task pane that shows your daily calendar agenda. The calendar also offers a 3-day view, which helps when you plan signing and funding days.
New Outlook suggests meeting times and includes a Scheduling Assistant. MailTips shows warnings before you send, so read them before you click send.

One known issue matters here. Events and contacts cannot be moved between accounts. If you keep a personal calendar and a work calendar, plan around that. The [calendar event guide](/how-to/create-a-calendar-event-in-outlook) covers the steps.
A worked example: one file from application to closing

Take one file. The borrower applies on Monday, and you send the status request template. The borrower returns statements on Wednesday, but one page is missing. You send the missing document follow-up template and snooze the thread until the borrower replies.

Underwriting then sends a condition letter. A rule moves the letter into the file folder. You add a reminder for the deadline. The title company asks for payoff figures, and you reply in the same thread with the closing instructions template.

Each step uses one tool. Templates handle repeat text. Snooze and reminders handle waiting. Rules handle sorting. Search finds the thread when the file goes sideways. Nothing in that chain is clever. It works because each piece is set up before the busy week starts.
The mistake is building this setup during a closing. Set up the templates and rules on a quiet day, then use them when the pressure arrives.
Mistakes that cost loan officers time in Outlook

items: Assuming accounts follow you between versions. They do not move on their own.
Deleting and re-adding an account to fix a glitch. One June 2026 Microsoft Q&A report says folders were scrambled after doing that.
Trusting a rule you never tested. Test it on a few old messages first.
Leaving borrower details in a saved template. Clear them out before you save.
Pasting full borrower files into any AI tool. Check your company's policy first.
Sending through a group address without a test. Send as and Send on behalf do not work with Office 365 Groups.

blocks.text: Each of these costs the most time on the day it matters. Fix the setup on a quiet afternoon instead.
Ask Lazur for help while you stay in Outlook

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a button is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. Lazur does not click for you and does not operate Outlook. You make every change yourself.
Hold fn to dictate. Clean, formatted text appears at the cursor in any app. Dictate a draft reply by voice, then read it before you send.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Borrower screens still need care, so check your company rules before you ask about a file.
Good first questions are short. Ask where the template option sits, or how to build a rule for title company mail. Ask Lazur to explain an underwriting condition in plain English.
Set up your Mac for the newest Outlook

Feature releases arrive often. Microsoft's release notes list Outlook 16.114, build 26101123, from Oct 14, 2026. It adds dynamic Microsoft 365 apps in the left rail and a choice of third-party online meeting providers when you create events. The latest listed build is 16.114.3, from Oct 27, 2026.

Your macOS version sets the limit. Microsoft says macOS 14 Sonoma is the minimum for updates to Microsoft 365 and Office. Apps on older macOS still run, but they get no updates, including security updates. Outlook 16.78 and later needs macOS 12 Monterey at minimum.
If your Mac runs an older system, ask your IT team about an upgrade before the next busy season. Check About This Mac first, so you know what you are running.
A weekly routine that keeps the inbox clear

items: Open My Day with Shift+⌘] and check the closings on your calendar.
Answer borrower replies first. Then move title and realtor threads to their folders.
Snooze conditions that wait on other people, and add a reminder for each deadline.
Send follow-up templates for any missing documents.
After any Outlook or macOS update, check the version and run a quick search test.

blocks.text: Once it is set up, the routine is short. The setup takes longer, so start it on a quiet day.
What to do next

Check your version today, then build the status request template. Next, add one rule for title company mail and test it. When you want help while you work, [download Lazur](/download) and hold ⌥ ⌘ in Outlook. You can compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: Should I switch to new Outlook for Mac or stay on legacy?
faq.answer: Use new Outlook for Mac. It is the default, and Microsoft says legacy support ends in October 2026. The new app adds features such as Snooze, nested compose, and Scheduling Assistant. Test your rules and search on a quiet day before you commit.

faq.question: Why don't I see templates in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Built-in templates need a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac 15.35 or later. Check the version under Outlook > About Outlook. The My Templates add-in needs an Exchange account and does not work in shared mailboxes. An admin may have turned add-ins off.

faq.question: Can Lazur send my emails from Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It points at things, guides you one click at a time, answers out loud, and drafts text. You review the text and send the email yourself.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin for Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It works in any app while you hold the shortcut, so you can ask about what is on screen in Outlook.

faq.question: Why would I use a shared mailbox for loan files?
faq.answer: A shared mailbox lets a processor or assistant work the same inbox as you. Add it with the shared mailbox guide. The My Templates add-in does not work there. Check Send as and Send on behalf before a deadline.

faq.question: What if search or rules stop working after the switch?
faq.answer: Some users reported that search, rules, and junk reporting did not work after the move. A Microsoft Q&A thread from June 2026 says so, and Microsoft staff did not reply in that thread. Test each feature on known messages. If one fails, ask your IT team to contact Microsoft support.
